recipes.name: Smoked Turkey Wild Rice Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 small inner stalk of celery with leaves, chopped

steps.text: Place turkey legs, water, bouillon cubes, onion, celery, carrots, garlic, bay leaves, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, thyme, marjoram, and curry powder in a soup pot; bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in wild rice. Simmer soup for at least 1 hour. Remove turkey legs; strip meat from the bones and tendons. Chop meat and return it to soup.
Pour in half-and-half and heat to just below a simmer; cook on low heat for about 30 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Smoked Turkey Wild Rice Soup
raw_recipe.description: A comforting bowl of creamy smoked turkey soup, full of vegetables and wild rice, makes a warm and fragrant meal when the cold winds blow.

review.reviewBody: This was a fantastic use for leftover turkey and a starting recipe base for me....... I started down that road because the instructions said to add the rice at two different points. I figured the second time was the right one. I also noticed there was no salt listed (the bouillon I used didn't add a salt taste at all for me)….so I went off on a tangent….The spice mix was very nice for this soup – but I added salt, Cajun seasoning, and red pepper. I added about 12 cups of water (I felt 8 was not enough for all the spices added!)…used dried celery leaf instead of the celery…used a tiny bit of red curry paste instead of the curry powder….. I used the two legs and two wings from our turkey. I diced my onions – didn’t want them in big pieces – since everything else was in small pieces! I brought to a boil and simmered for 30 minutes. Then I took out the turkey and removed the meat and returned the meat to the pot. I then added 1 quart of buttermilk (instead of the half and half), one cup of our leftover mashed potatoes, and one small can mushroom pieces (drained)……..and brought to a simmer and maintained on low for 30 minutes. I then added 1 cup Minute Rice and ½ cup “Egg Bow” pasta and simmered for 20 minutes. Came out wonderful! Oh – also – even though it’s common sense – the recipe should mention to remove the bay leaves before serving! I do love the combination of the spices – so don’t shy from this recipe – just needed a few tweaks for me!!!!

This was delicious!! The only thing I did different was use one pint of cream instead. I did taste it before adding the cream and whoa it's salty!! The cream definitely cuts the salt!! I also used egg noodles instead of rice and added white rice on the side (love my starch!!) 

Next time I will add the veggies a tad bit later, after all the simmering, the veggies were mush. I think I'll also throw out some of the broth after boiling and then add fresh water to omit some of the salt in the broth because I was parched after eating it!! 

It makes a big pot but worth the leftovers!! This will be great after thanksgiving!!

Great soup! I roasted the Turkey legs and left out the half and half to make it healthier. Used homemade turkey broth. Used half the curry called for because my husband isn't a curry fan. Took others advice and added some red pepper flakes. Husband said this may be the best soup I have made. Next time I think we will go with the full curry. I doubled the recipie as we like to freeze portions for quick meal after work. Was great re-heated.

Awesome soup! I doubled the curry because we love the flavor it brings to poultry. I used the smoked carcass to make the broth, then added chunks of breast meat to give it more substance. I personally thought the recipe was perfect just the way it is, but my wife would have liked it better if I left out the cream. I thought it was great both ways!

What a wonderful soup! So rich and satifying. I prepared this with leftover slow-cooked turkey breast, just cubed and added a few drops of liquid smoke for a delicious smokey taste. I doubled the curry, wow, the curry really makes this soup. Also used a cup or so of heavy cream instead of the published amount of 1/2 & 1/2, as that's what I had on hand. Highly recommended & a definite do-over. Thanks for sharing your recipe with AR.

I used my own turkey broth after grilling (and using apple wood chips) a turkey breast. The flavor from the chips was lovely, and no chemicals. I sauteed the veggies, including sliced baby portabella mushrooms, to add that texture to the soup, and simmered 1/2 hour less. Loved the combination of spices!

HOLY SMOKES! This soup is rich, smoky, creamy, and so satisfying. Never have I ever had anything like it! I followed the recipe, but instead of using one cup of dry wild rice, I used two of those 8.5-ounce pre-cooked wild rice and quinoa medley packets. I simply added them in in the last fifteen minutes of cooking, shortly after the half and half. I have to admit, this soup is VERY smoky and very salty - however, that is the very nature of a smoked turkey leg. I recommend cutting down on the chicken bouillon to one or two cubes instead of four. Regardless, this one is a keeper.

I made this exactly as the recipe...except used 1/2 teaspoon of pepper, no curry and put it in the crock pot for 8 hours on low then added the half and half the last hour. This came out so delicious! It's a keeper....and now I know what to do with our leftover smoked turkey legs.

I made this recipe today. For a little extra flavor also added 1/2 cup parmesan cheese, and couple teaspoons of of minced garlic, as well as extra panco for that crunch. This turned out great. I'll made this again.
Used multigrain rice and 1 1/2 tsp. Curry then added diced red pepper. Delicious!
this soup was delicious! I only used half the quart of half-and-half and it was plenty creamy. Also, I added leftover chopped turkey to the soup when I added the rice. Will definitely make again!

We had smoked our first turkey and of course had left overs. This soup was really tasty. I think the cream settled down the smoky flavor. I loved that everything for the recipe was in my pantry. I would absolutely make this again. I didn't change the recipe at all.

This is a hit with the entire extended family. I make this every year since the one year we had a smoked turkey, maybe 5 years ago? I've just used roasted turkey in subsequent years, I do use the curry, no other substitutions except maybe leftover green beans. Various relatives have stopped by the day I make the soup and I knew they liked it but - before T'giving a relative asked if I was going to make the soup. We had 21 at dinner and 2 more relatives asked about the soup and it turned into a discussion among all the adults and teens about who missed out last year and who was first in line or most deserving this year. I'm making the soup today and am going to add a dash of smoke flavoring because my favorite version was the year I used smoked turkey.

I also felt it was too salty the first day, yet I admit I didn't have a quart of half n half to use. I used about 1 c 1/2 1/2 and then some 2% milk. The second day and thereafter it didn't seem as / too salty yet that may have been tolerance. Overall I think it is a great soup. I used stock (not bullion) and added wild mushrooms. I will make this again. I really liked the thyme, marjoram, curry, wild rice combo.

I made this recipe as written except I did not add the curry and all of the half and half (maybe a cup). I also used half of the broth from the carcass of the turkey I smoked and the remaining water. The only thing I'd do different next time is use half of the black pepper. To me the black pepper really overpowered the soup. Otherwise, very good recipe and I got to use up the smoked turkey.
probably the best Turkey soup I've ever made, the only thing I did differently was add green beans.
Made this according to the recipe using Winco Bistro Rice Blend. Served it in homemade bread bowls.
I made this with my leftover Smoked Turkey carcass and it is SO GOOD. I didn't have any half-and-half so ate it without it and still amazing.
This was amazing — period. If you are getting bad results, look over your methods. We are blown away at how good this is.
